Embedded & hardware security

Wireless and IoT Protocol Analysis

Planned notes on analyzing wireless IoT traffic across BLE, Zigbee, LoRa/LoRaWAN, and Sub-GHz links, including experiments with basic SDR equipment.

To be continued…

Planned scope

This planned work will examine wireless IoT communication beyond Wi-Fi, including BLE, Zigbee, LoRa, LoRaWAN, and Sub-GHz RF. Proposed experiments include traffic analysis and SDR work with HackRF or RTL-SDR.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Lab setup and spectrum hygiene

  • Define the owned devices and shielded test conditions.
  • Record regulatory limits and transmit power.
  • Log equipment, antennas, and sample rates.

BLE analysis

  • Capture advertising and connection traffic.
  • Map services, characteristics, and pairing behavior.
  • Document encryption and authentication observations.

Zigbee and Sub-GHz

  • Capture join and control traffic on a test network.
  • Identify frame formats and repeated payloads.
  • Record channel, PAN ID, and key configuration.

LoRa and LoRaWAN

  • Capture uplink and downlink frames.
  • Inspect join procedure and payload structure.
  • State what can and cannot be inferred without keys.

Findings and references

  • Compare protocol behavior with the specification.
  • Record defensive recommendations for owned deployments.
  • Link the relevant standards and tool documentation.

Topics to cover

  • BLE
  • Zigbee
  • LoRa and LoRaWAN
  • Sub-GHz RF
  • HackRF and RTL-SDR
